subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for ZenHealth - next steps
messages:
From: Sophie Park <sophie@zenhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery call scheduling

Thanks for taking the time today, Marissa — really helpful intro. A quick note to confirm our priorities and the items we covered so we can align internally.

Pain points we described:
- Current latency spikes when batch jobs run, and unpredictable tail latency during peak business hours.
- Token costs are rising quickly with our current hosted provider; we need predictable unit economics.
- Regulatory requirement: isolation of PHI inference workloads and customer key management (KMS/HSM).

Current stack summary (from our side):
- Models: custom fine-tuned Llama-2 family for clinical summarization (on-prem and in-cloud replicas).
- Inference: currently using multi-tenant hosted endpoints with autoscaling; orchestration via Kubernetes.
- Throughput: baseline 1200 TPS during business hours, peak bursts up to ~3500 TPS for short windows.
- SLOs: 99th percentile latency target of 250ms for streaming summaries.

Success criteria we mentioned:
1) Dedicated GPU pool with strong isolation for PHI workloads.
2) Predictable cost & throughput for baseline traffic and a predictable autoscaling/burst policy for peaks.
3) Integration with our KMS + audit logs and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Next steps from our side:
- Internal alignment on capacity budget and security signoff (procurement looped).
- Please send a brief recap with recommended sizing and what Dedicated would look like operationally.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Park
Head of ML Ops, ZenHealth
Sophie.Park@zenhealth.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@zenhealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@zenhealth.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@zenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for ZenHealth - next steps

Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and for the time today. Recapping our discovery and outlining a proposed Dedicated capacity fit for ZenHealth below.

Quick highlights / confirmation of pain points (same as you listed):
- Unpredictable tail latency and cost spikes
- Need for PHI isolation and KMS integration
- Baseline throughput ~1200 TPS, peak bursts to ~3500 TPS

Recommended Dedicated configuration (initial proposal):
- Dedicated GPU pools: 8 x A100-style nodes for baseline (targeting ~1200 sustained TPS with <200ms median latency for your model family).
- Burst/autoscale policy: warm standby pool that can scale up to additional 6 nodes within 5-10 minutes (estimated headroom for ~3500 TPS during short peaks).
- Isolation: single-tenant VPC for PHI workloads + optional on-prem connector for air-gapped inference.
- Security: KMS/HSM integration for key management, full audit logs, SOC2 artifacts available.
- Cost controls: per-pool quotas + token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards to monitor unit economics.

Technical notes / assumptions to validate with your engineers:
- Model sequence length distribution: assumed 512 tokens average; if you commonly hit >1024 we need to adjust node sizing.
- KV cache hit rate: assumed 30% for clinical summarization patterns — higher cache hit reduces node count.
- Acceptable cold-start behavior for burst windows: can tolerate 5-10 minute ramp with warm pool.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Rafael (our solutions engineer) to validate model perf numbers and sizing — Rafael, can you share your availability for a 60-minute session this week?
2) We'll share a draft commercial outline including subscription for Dedicated pool + estimated monthly cost and a separate line for optional on-prem connector and compliance package.
3) We can provide SOC2 evidence and a short security questionnaire (we have a completed SOC2 pack ready).

Attachments: ZenHealth-SLA-requirements.pdf (procurement example), zenhealth-current-architecture.png (what we captured from the call).

Thanks — copying Rafael and Vanessa to pick up scheduling and SOW/commercial items.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0218

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sophie Park <sophie@zenhealth.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@zenhealth.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for ZenHealth - next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from Product/Infra: 
- Can dedicated pools be pinned to specific regions (we have data residency needs across US-East and US-West)?
- For the burst policy, do you support per-customer pre-warmed capacity (paid reservation) vs. purely on-demand scaling? We are open to a hybrid so we can guarantee short-term spikes.
- KMS: we need to confirm whether Redwood supports our AWS KMS key and whether HSM-backed keys are supported.

Also: for procurement, can you include the high-level SLA targets (p99 latency, availability SLA) and the standard penalty/credits language? We'll need that to move budget approval.

If you can share the tech-deep-dive calendar invite and a short draft commercial, we can get procurement and security to review in parallel.

Cheers,
Liam
Senior Product Manager, ZenHealth

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenhealth.com>, Sophie Park <sophie@zenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for ZenHealth - next steps

Hi Liam / Sophie — Rafael here, Solutions Engineering. Thanks for the detailed questions — quick answers and proposed agenda for the technical deep-dive: 

Answers:
- Region pinning: yes, Dedicated pools can be deployed to specific regions (we support multi-region deployments and can mirror pools for residency).
- Burst policy: we support hybrid models — reserved pre-warmed capacity (paid reservation) + on-demand autoscale for additional short bursts. We typically propose a small reserved warm pool sized for critical short bursts to meet tight SLOs.
- KMS/HSM: we support bringing your AWS KMS keys and can offer HSM-backed key management integrations; we'll need a short connectivity checklist to validate white-listed egress for key operations.
- SLA language: Marissa will include the standard SLA summary (availability % and p99 latency target) in the draft commercial; we can discuss specific credit terms with legal if required.

Proposed tech deep-dive agenda (60-75 minutes):
1) Quick re-cap of workload characteristics (sequence lengths, KV cache patterns, model size) — 10 min
2) Live perf profiling: Rafael to run a small perf test with a sample request trace (if you can share a sanitized trace) — 25 min
3) Sizing and autoscale policy options (warm pool sizing, scale-out times) — 15 min
4) Security & networking checklist (KMS, VPC peering, audit logs) — 10 min
5) Next steps & action items — 5 min

Suggested times this week: Tue 6/16 10:00-11:15 PT or Wed 6/17 09:00-10:15 PT. Rafael will send a calendar invite once you confirm preferred slot and whether you can share a small sanitized perf trace.

Action items I will take after the call: sample perf run results + a short sizing spreadsheet mapping pool count to expected TPS / p99 latency.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
